event: 2026 ILCA SENIOR EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS & OPEN EUROPEAN TROPHY
procedural_matters: HUN 213119 was represented by Jonatan Vadnai.
CRO 216061 was represented by Filip Jurisic.
The race committee was represented by Francisco Sg Jauregui (EurILCA Course Representative).
Hearing No. 11 was heard together with hearing No. 12 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since both hearings arose from the same incident.

The protest time limit for the ILCA 7 Men Yellow fleet was 16:00. CRO 216061 delivered the request for redress at 16:02. As CRO 216061 came back ashore, she took the boat out of the water, and immediately went to his phone and filed the request for redress.

CRO 216061 failed to deliver the request for redress within the protest time limit, as required by RRS 61.2(b)(1). However, there was good reason for the international jury to extend the time limit. Therefore the request for redress is valid under RRS 61.3.
Noela Petesic (International Jury) attended the hearing as an observer.
Jozo Jakelic (Coach CRO), Mate Arapov (Coach CRO), Lovre Perhat (Coach AUT) gave evidence as a witness for CRO.
Ilko Klakor (Coach MNE) gave evidence as a witness for HUN.
Denis Marinov (Course Race Officer) gave evidence as a witness for the race committee.
The race committee presented an audio recording during the hearing.
facts: The race committee displayed the black flag as the preparatory signal during the second attempt to start race 4.
The race committee is sighting the line sitting in front of the mast, behind the staff where the orange flag is displayed.
The race committee did not identify any boats in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark during the last minute before the starting signal.
The EurILCA Course Representative confirmed on the radio 3 seconds after the start that it was a clear start.
Both boats stated during the hearing that they had a feeling that a lot of boats were over the starting line.
HUN 213119 sailed and finished race 4 in 10th place.
CRO 216061 sailed and finished race 4 in 14th place.
conclusions: A race committee member sighting the starting line is better placed than any competing boat to decide whether a boat was over the line at the starting signal (see WS Case 136).
There was neither an improper action nor improper omission of the race committee. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
